confidence_definitions.high: Judgments rest on high-quality, corroborated information from multiple independent sources; the reasoning admits few plausible alternatives.
confidence_definitions.low: Judgments rest on fragmentary, uncorroborated or questionable information, or on significant assumptions; alternatives are as plausible as the judgment.
confidence_definitions.moderate: Judgments rest on credible but incompletely corroborated information, or on sound reasoning from limited information; alternative explanations remain plausible.

rules.evidence_required: Note whether the draft states its assumptions and reasoning explicitly and avoids loaded or one-sided language.
rules.text: Analysts must perform their functions with objectivity and with awareness of their own assumptions and reasoning. They must employ reasoning techniques and practical mechanisms that reveal and mitigate bias.
rules.title: Objective

rules.evidence_required: Note any passage that advocates a policy outcome rather than assessing a situation.
rules.text: Analytic assessments must not be distorted by, nor shaped for, advocacy of a particular audience, agenda, or policy viewpoint.
rules.title: Independent of political consideration

rules.evidence_required: Timeliness cannot be judged from the text alone; attest and note the date range of the sources if the draft states one.
rules.text: Analysis must be disseminated in time to be actionable by customers.
rules.title: Timely

rules.evidence_required: Every provided source is either cited by at least one claim or explicitly set aside in the scope note with a reason, and the gaps section names the information that is missing.
rules.text: Analysis should be informed by all relevant information available. Analytic elements should identify and address critical information gaps.
rules.title: Based on all available sources of intelligence information

rules.evidence_required: Pass when every verifiable icd203.tc.* rule passes; otherwise fail and list the failing tradecraft standards.
rules.text: Analytic products must implement and exhibit the nine analytic tradecraft standards.
rules.title: Implements and exhibits analytic tradecraft standards

rules.evidence_required: The sources section has one entry per source with a descriptor from the lexicon and a reliability note that addresses at least currency and completeness.
rules.text: Analytic products should identify underlying sources and methodologies on which judgments are based, and use source descriptors to describe factors affecting source quality and credibility, such as accuracy and completeness, possible denial and deception, age and continued currency of information, and technical elements of collection.
rules.title: Properly describes quality and credibility of underlying sources, data, and methodologies

rules.evidence_required: Every key judgment carries a confidence level; every judgment claim uses a likelihood term from the lexicon and no other probability wording; the basis for uncertainty is stated.
rules.text: Analytic products should indicate and explain the basis for the uncertainties associated with major analytic judgments, specifically the likelihood of occurrence of an event or development, and the analyst's confidence in the basis for this judgment. Products should use the standard terms of likelihood and should not combine a confidence level and a degree of likelihood in the same sentence.
rules.title: Properly expresses and explains uncertainties associated with major analytic judgments

rules.evidence_required: Each claim's kind (fact, judgment, assumption) matches its wording; every assumption is stated as such in the analysis and its implication is given.
rules.text: Analytic products should clearly distinguish statements that convey underlying intelligence information used in analysis from statements that convey assumptions or judgments. Assumptions should be explicitly stated and their implications for the analysis explained.
rules.title: Properly distinguishes between underlying intelligence information and analysts' assumptions and judgments

rules.evidence_required: At least one alternative hypothesis is stated and assessed whenever any key judgment is below high confidence; each alternative says why it is less likely than the judgment.
rules.text: Analysis of alternatives is the systematic evaluation of differing hypotheses to explain events or phenomena, explore near-term outcomes, and imagine possible futures. Analytic products should identify and assess plausible alternative hypotheses, particularly when major judgments carry significant uncertainty or when a hypothesis would have major consequences if it proved true.
rules.title: Incorporates analysis of alternatives

rules.evidence_required: The key judgments answer the value statement the analyst supplied, name the audience it serves, and state what the judgments imply for that audience.
rules.text: Analytic products should provide information and insight on issues relevant to the customers and address the implications of the information and analysis they provide.
rules.title: Demonstrates customer relevance and addresses implications

rules.evidence_required: Key judgments come first; each analysis paragraph ties to the claims it supports; no paragraph contradicts a key judgment; sentences are unambiguous.
rules.text: Analytic products should present a clear main analytic message up front. Products should provide the key reasons for the main analytic message and show how the evidence supports the judgments. Language and syntax should convey meaning unambiguously.
rules.title: Uses clear and logical argumentation

rules.evidence_required: Corelata v1 has no memory of prior reports; attest, and note whether the scope note says this is initial coverage.
rules.text: Analytic products should state how their major judgments on a topic are consistent with or represent a change from those in previously published analysis, or represent initial coverage of a topic.
rules.title: Explains change to or consistency of analytic judgments

with_prior_reports.evidence_required: INPUT_JSON.prior_reports holds the key judgments of this project's earlier accepted reports. Pass when the draft's changes_from_previous says, for each earlier judgment on the topic of one of its key judgments, whether the draft is consistent with it or changes it and why, and states the earlier judgment accurately; or when no earlier judgment bears on the draft's topic and the scope note says this is initial coverage. Fail when a key judgment departs from an earlier judgment on its topic without saying so, when an entry misstates the earlier judgment, or when an entry claims a change or a consistency the judgments do not show.

rules.evidence_required: Every claim cites at least one source unit whose text actually supports it; no judgment claims more than its cited units allow. Cite the claim ids and unit refs you checked.
rules.text: Analytic products should apply expertise and logic to make the most accurate judgments and assessments possible, based on the information available and known information gaps. Judgments should not be overstated or understated relative to the evidence.
rules.title: Makes accurate judgments and assessments

rules.evidence_required: Corelata v1 generates no visuals; attest. A profile may make this verifiable once a deployment renders charts or maps.
rules.text: Analytic products should incorporate visual information to clarify an analytic message and to complement or enhance the presentation of data and analysis.
rules.title: Incorporates effective visual information where appropriate

rules.evidence_required: The source summary states the strengths and weaknesses of the source base, names the sources the key judgments depend on most, and names the sources that corroborate or conflict with one another (or says that none conflict). A report without a source_summary section may give this summary in its scope note or sources section.
rules.text: Source summary statements are strongly encouraged in covered analytic products to provide a holistic assessment of sourcing that supports a covered analytic product. A source summary statement should cover strengths and weaknesses of the source base, which sources are most important to key judgments, what sources are meaningfully corroborative or conflicting, and should highlight any specific subject matter expertise used to develop the assessment.
rules.title: Source summary statement present

rules.evidence_required: Every key judgment lists claim ids, and every one of those claims cites source units.
rules.text: Analytic judgments shall be supported by source reference citations that allow the reader to identify the specific reporting behind each judgment.
rules.title: Source reference citations for key judgments

rules.evidence_required: Every entry in the sources section uses a descriptor from the lexicon's source_descriptors.
rules.text: Source descriptors shall use consistent, approved terminology so that readers across products understand source type and reliability the same way.
rules.title: Source descriptors from the approved lexicon
